locator: Abstract and method overview; ACM SIGKDD 2004
evidence_summary: The original feature-based opinion-mining study frames review summarization around product features, sentences expressing opinions on those features, and orientation of the opinions.
limitations: The official ACM landing record was not readable in the research client; R02-S02, by the same researcher, provides the later formal exposition. They are not independent support for this lineage.
notes: Original source identity verified; use R02-S02 for detailed tuple semantics.

evidence_summary: Liu defines opinions over an entity or an entity–aspect pair and gives an opinion quintuple containing entity, aspect, sentiment, holder, and time. It distinguishes target referent from the textual expression that may name it.
supports: opinion target is more than a polarity label
limitations: A conceptual formulation, not a current shared-task data specification.
notes: Used for terminology and relation distinctions, not as a final REVIEW² model.

evidence_summary: The monograph describes entity hierarchies containing parts and attributes, then notes that a simplified two-level treatment calls both parts and attributes ‘aspects’; it also notes varying conventions for aspect, feature, facet, attribute, and topic.
supports: aspect is not automatically a catalog property
limitations: The source simplifies terminology for opinion mining; it does not specify a product-catalog ontology.
notes: Directly motivates separation of R02 aspect terminology from R01 property identity.

evidence_summary: The source separates direct, indirect, regular, and comparative opinions, and treats an objective statement that implies an evaluation as an implicit opinion; it notes that implicit opinions have received less attention than explicit ones.
supports: factual-looking statements can carry evaluative implications
limitations: Its implicit-opinion framing is broader than any one ABSA benchmark annotation rule.
notes: Do not infer an implicit target without recording that it was inferred.

locator: pp. 47–49, objective/subjective sentences and sentence-level assumptions
evidence_summary: The source explains that objective sentences can imply sentiment and subjective sentences need not be evaluative; it also shows that one sentence may contain different opinions on multiple aspects, invalidating a single holder/sentiment assumption for the whole sentence.
limitations: Examples are explanatory, not a general conflict-resolution rule.
notes: Supports not collapsing a review sentence to one sentiment label.

evidence_summary: The source represents comparative opinions using compared entities, an aspect, a preferred entity, holder, and time; comparison orders entities with respect to shared aspects rather than assigning a standalone polarity.
limitations: The sextuple is a conceptual formulation and does not resolve entity identity across product catalogs.
notes: Cross-checked against the original comparative paper R02-S05.

locator: p. 1, Introduction, lines 47–70 in official PDF
evidence_summary: SemEval-2014 contrasts overall sentiment with aspect-based analysis, using a laptop review that contains positive and negative evaluations of different aspects and objective information. It defines ABSA as identifying reviewed-entity aspects and their sentiment.
supports: objective information is not simply polarity
limitations: 2014 task formulation is domain/dataset scoped and does not model holder, comparison, or product identity level as general slots.
notes: Official task definition.

evidence_summary: SemEval-2016 sentence-level ABSA defines opinion tuples with Aspect Category as a predefined entity E and attribute A pair, an Opinion Target Expression as the text expression referring to E, and a positive/negative/neutral polarity label.
limitations: The predefined inventories are domain-specific; an OTE is a text span, not a stable product entity identifier.
notes: Official task field definition.

evidence_summary: The SemEval-2016 OTE is recorded by character offsets and takes the value null when the reviewed entity has no explicit mention in the text.
limitations: Null OTE records missing explicit entity mention, not a resolved implicit aspect identity or confidence.
notes: Useful counterexample to forcing every category into a text span.

evidence_summary: SemEval-2022 Structured Sentiment Analysis requires prediction of sentiment graphs; each opinion graph has a holder, target, expression, and polarity, with relations among those elements.
limitations: The task is not product-review-specific and does not require product property/category or product-identity hierarchy fields.
notes: Official shared-task definition, not a schema recommendation.

evidence_summary: Phrase-level contextual polarity is affected by local and non-local negation, intensifiers, diminishers, modality including realis/irrealis, word sense, and syntactic context; the annotation distinguishes positive, negative, neutral, and both cases.
limitations: Linguistic contextual polarity is not a model of physical usage condition or evidence reliability.
notes: Use modifiers and reliability as separate analytical layers.

locator: p. 1, Abstract and Introduction; pp. 2–4 annotation scheme
evidence_summary: MPQA 3.0 adds entity and event targets to a span-annotated opinion corpus. It notes that review-corpus targets are often product/service aspects and limited, and that prior corpora commonly considered only writer sentiment rather than sentiment attributed to other entities.
supports: target not limited to product aspect
limitations: MPQA is general-domain opinion annotation, not a product identity or review-comparison standard.
notes: Supports holder/source and target distinctions without assuming its corpus format is universal.

evidence_summary: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction jointly extracts target/aspect terms, their sentiment, and opinion spans that explain the sentiment, producing linked triplets rather than isolated aspect and polarity labels.
limitations: The triplet has no standard holder, comparative, measurement, or product-variant slot.
notes: Used for the semantic-unit structure, not model-performance claims.

evidence_summary: Aspect Sentiment Quad Prediction identifies four elements in a quad: aspect category, aspect term, opinion term, and sentiment, and treats their joint recovery as one task.
limitations: Category and aspect-term semantics are dataset-defined; no product ontology mapping is supplied.
notes: Shows that modern structured extraction can preserve both category and surface term.

evidence_summary: ACOS quadruple extraction targets aspect-category–opinion–sentiment quads and explicitly includes implicit aspects and implicit opinions in its task setting.
limitations: The source establishes a task formulation, not a universally reliable method for resolving an omitted property.
notes: Supports explicitness as a candidate status, not automatic inference.

evidence_summary: Comparative opinion mining defines comparative sentences as expressing an ordering relation between entities with respect to a common feature and seeks to identify and extract the associated comparison relations.
limitations: The task does not establish a universal product-entity resolution or recommendation model.
notes: Original comparative study; corroborates but is not independently summed with R02-S02's retelling.

locator: p. 19, opinion quintuple limitations and context example
evidence_summary: The monograph explicitly states that its opinion quintuple does not cover context and gives a tall-person condition in a car-size evaluation as an example of omitted context.
limitations: One formalization and example; it is not a taxonomy of user, task, activity, or environment.
notes: Important negative finding: an opinion tuple alone need not capture applicability conditions.

evidence_summary: The targeted ABSA model uses textual context to improve target-aspect sentiment classification, demonstrating that surrounding language can matter for interpreting a target/aspect evaluation.
limitations: This is a model-specific treatment of textual context; it does not define physical/social context-of-use dimensions.
notes: The report treats its context use as discourse/textual, not as R03 context-of-use evidence.

evidence_summary: The paper proposes generating a product aspect hierarchy from unstructured consumer reviews with domain assistance, in order to organize review information hierarchically.
supports: hierarchy is generated rather than canonical
limitations: A learned/domain-assisted hierarchy is not a governed product classification or multilingual terminology standard.
notes: Used to reject automatic equivalence with R01 product-property hierarchy.

evidence_summary: The HASM paper discovers a hierarchical aspect–sentiment tree from unlabeled online reviews; each node represents an aspect and its children represent associated sentiment polarities.
limitations: The hierarchy is inferred from review text and word distributions, not a universal aspect vocabulary.
notes: A second, non-mirror example that hierarchical structures occur in ABSA research.

evidence_summary: The paper models intra- and inter-sentence review structure because sentences in a review elaborate on one another and surrounding discourse can inform aspect-based sentiment classification.
limitations: It models review text structure, not user/task/environment or comparison/conflict semantics.
notes: Used only to distinguish textual/discourse context from R03 scope.

evidence_summary: The recommender paper mines aspect-sentiment pairs and separately models user attention and item property for rating estimation; it treats the pairs as aspect-level evidence rather than defining recommendation as a core ABSA tuple element.
limitations: A recommender-system application paper, not a shared ABSA annotation standard for recommendation statements.
notes: Supports leaving recommendation/preference as unresolved rather than a core field.
